Laura —

Thanks for looping us in. Given Amaranth is not SST-registered and they’re invoicing from a Malaysia entity, two operational items for finance and tax: 

1) We need to confirm whether our payment should treat the invoice as subject to any local withholding or reverse-charge accounting. Malaysia’s treatment for cross-border digital/IT services can vary by place of supply and whether the services are effectively exported. Rishi — can you confirm the treatment and whether we need a TRC or gross-up / withholding clause in the PO?

2) If we can’t obtain an SST certificate or TRC, we should include a payment hold trigger: finance will hold the payment until vendor provides either (a) a TRC, or (b) evidence that services are supplied from outside Malaysia. That avoids downstream tax exposure.

We should also prepare a short clause in the PO requiring vendor cooperation with tax documentation requests and agreeing to reimburse any withholding/redirection costs if incorrect declarations are made.

Happy to draft PO language.

—Ben

Hi all —

Thanks, Nurul. I reviewed the attached declaration. High-level guidance (not formal opinion):

- If the supplier is invoicing from a Malaysian-registered legal entity and provides services physically or economically consumed in Malaysia, SST could apply. If their operations and invoicing are effectively outbound (services supplied from Singapore) and Malaysia branch is acting as an invoicing conduit without taxable supply, then SST may not apply. Evidence matters.
- Tax residency certificate (TRC) is helpful but not always determinative; a Singapore tax residency certificate for the parent can support an exported-services position.
- If we cannot establish exported-service treatment, there is risk of local service tax or withholding at the point of payment. To protect Redwood, include the following in the PO: (a) vendor warranties on SST/TRC status; (b) indemnity for any local tax assessed on Redwood due to incorrect declarations; and (c) an agreement to provide a TRC within 30 days of first invoice.

I attached a short internal memo summarizing our approach: redwood_tax_opinion_malaysia.pdf.

Next steps I recommend:
- Laura: request TRC or parent Singapore tax residency certificate and the signed vendor form (DocuSign).
- Finance: prepare PO with the three clauses above and a payment hold/clearance step.
- Nurul: if possible, provide an invoice sample showing billing party and origin of services.

Happy to jump on a quick call if needed.

—Rishi
